la:noun:testamentum.html:
testāmentum, i, n.
testor
,
the publication of a last will or testament; a will, testament (cf. codicilli).
In gen., sqq.: testamentum est voluntatis nostrae justa sententia de eo, quod quis post mortem suam fieri velit,: testamentum legere ... obsignare ... facere,; ; cf.: testamenti factio,: testamenti factionem habere,: testamentum conscribere,: obsignare,; : signare,: mutare,; : rumpere,; ; cf.: testamentorum ruptorum aut ratorum jura,: constat agnascendo rumpi testamentum,; sqq.: irritum facere,: subicere,; ; cf.: testamentorum subjector,: supponere,; cf. : testamento cavere aliquid,: testamento esse in triente,: eripis hereditatem, quae venerat testamento,: cum ex testamento HS. milies relinquatur,: testamenta resignare,: testamento aliquem adoptare,: testamenta nuncupare, to announce or acknowledge before witnesses, ; .—Concerning the three different kinds of testaments (calatis comitiis, per aes ad libram, and in procinctu), and the laws relating to wills in gen., v. Lübker, Real-Lex., s.v. Testamentum, and esp. Rein, Privatr. p. 363 sq.—
In eccl. Lat: Testamentum vetus et novum, the Old and New Testaments, cf. ; : vetus,: novum,.

la:noun:testis.html:
testis, is, comm. (
neutr. form: caelum teste vocat,), one who attests any thing (orally or in writing), a witness (cf. superstes): testes vinctos attines,: pluris est oculatus testis unus quam auriti decem,: deos absentes testes memoras,: vosque, dii, testes facio,: deos hominesque se testes facere,: deūm, quos testes foederum invocabant consules,: ut manus ad caelum tendens deos testes ingrati animi Magnetum invocaret,; ; ; : apud me ut apud bonum judicem argumenta plus quam testes valent,: si negem ... quo me teste convinces?: satis idonei testes et conscii,; so, cupidi, conjurati et ab religione remoti,: religiosus,: incorrupti atque integri,: graves, leves,: locupletissimi, et saep.: dabo tibi testis nec nimis antiquos nec ullo modo barbaros,; so, testes dare in aliquam rem,: proferre,: adhibere,: citare in aliquam rem,, §146: ut iis testibus in summā pecuniae uteretur,; cf. : testibus uti,; ; . — With dependent-clause: testis faciet ilico, Vendidisse me,: iis utimini testibus appropinquare eorum adventum,, cf. . — Fem.: Venus Cyrenensis, testem te testor mihi,: teste deā, (17), 124: nutrix testis fida doloris,: musa mea,: inductā teste in senatu, Haec, inquit, etc.,.—Of things: sidera sunt testes et matutina pruina,: quid debeas, o Roma Neronibus, Testis Metaurum flumen et Hasdrubal Devictus, etc.,: testis mecum est anulus,.—
Transf., an eye-witness, spectator, i. q. arbiter (rare; cf. also conscius): facies bona teste caret,: puduitque gementem, Illo teste mori,: ac lunā teste moventur,.

la:noun:testa.gloss: a piece of burned clay, brick, tile
senses: a piece of burned clay, brick, tile
a sort of clapping with the flat of the hands (as if with two tiles), in token of applause, invented by Nero
la:noun:testa.html:
testa, ae, f.
= tosta, from torreo
,
a piece of burned clay, a brick, tile, ὄστρακον.
Lit., ; ; ; ; ; ; ; .—
Transf.
A piece of baked earthen-ware, an earthen pot, pitcher, jug, urn, etc. (cf. testu): si Prometheus ... a vicinis cum testā ambulans carbunculos corrogaret,: testā cum ardente viderent Scintillare oleum,a lamp,: quo semel est imbuta recens, servabit odorem Testa diu,; cf. : accipiat Manes parvula testa meos, (3, 5, 16): vinum Graeca quod testā conditum levi,; : mihi fundat avitum Condita testa merum,; ; ; ; .—Used in applause: audiat ille Testarum crepitus cum verbis, (cf. F. infra).—
A broken piece of earthen-ware, pottery, brick, etc.; a sherd, potsherd: dissipatis imbricum fragminibus ac testis tegularum, Sisenn. ap. : testa parem fecit,: fulcitur testā mensa,; ; ; ; ; .—Hence,
Transf., a piece of bone, ; so of fragments of a broken tooth, ; .—
Like ὄστρακον,a sherd, potsherd, in the ostracism or judicial voting of the Greeks: testarum suffragiis, quod illi ὀστρακισμὸν vocant, ; cf. also testula.—
The shell of shell-fish or of testaceous animals: genera beluarum ad saxa nativis testis inhaerentium,: ostreae,: muricum,: cochlearum,: testudinis, Müll. —Hence,
Transf.
A shell-fish: non omne mare generosae fertile testae,: marina,.—
A shell or covering, in gen.: lubricaque immotas testa premebat aquas,i. e. an icy shell, covering of ice,: lubrica, Poët. ap. Burm.—
The skull: testa hominis, nudum jam cute calvitium,; Prud. στεφ. 10, 761; ; fin. (hence, Ital. testa and Fr. tēte).—
A brick-colored spot on the face, ; . 12, 50, § 185.—
A sort of clapping with the flat of the hands (as if with two tiles), in token of applause, invented by Nero, .

la:noun:testu.html:
testu or testum, i, n.
testa
,
a vessel or lid which was placed over food, etc., to be cooked, and then covered with hot coals, usually of earthenware.
Lit.: in foco caldo sub testu coquito leniter,: sub testu,; cf.: et fumant testu pressus uterque suo,: fimo ovium sub testo calefacto,: unguito focum, ubi coquas, colfacito bene et testum,.—Abl. testo, ; ; .— Afterwards of metal: ranarum corda sub aereo testo discoxere,.—
Transf., an earthen vessel, earthen pot: ara fit: huc ignem curto fert rustica testu,; ; Mumm. and Afran. ap. P.

la:noun:testimonium.html:
testĭmōnĭum, ii, n.
testor
,
witness, evidence, attestation, testimony (oral or written): qui falsas lites falsis testimoniis Petunt,: testimonii dictio,: quorum egregiam fuisse virtutem testimonio Ciceronis cognoverat,: testimonium in aliquem dicere,; testimonium dicere de conjuratione,: testimonium dicere contra deos,; cf.: dicere aliquid pro testimonio,; ; ; : testimonium impertire,: Bruttiano justissimum integritatis testimonium redditum,: licet iis testimonium reddere industriae, : Publio tuo neque operā ... neque testimonio defui,: legite testimonia testium vestrorum,: testimonia recitare, Hadrian. in ; so, falsi testes, falsa signa testimoniaque et indicia ex eādem officinā exibant,: vocare aliquem ad testimonium,: citare ad testimonium,: in testimonium citare,: ovis damnata falso testimonio,.—
Transf., that which serves as proof of any thing, proof, evidence: hoc interest inter exemplum et testimonium: exemplo demonstratur, id quod dicimus cujusmodi sit: testimonio, esse illud ita, ut nos dicimus, confirmatur,: testimoniorum quae sunt genera? Divinum et humanum: divinum, ut oracula, ut auspicia, ut vaticinationes et responsa sacerdotum, haruspicum, conjectorum: humanum, quod spectatur ex auctoritate et ex voluntate et ex oratione aut liberā aut expressā: in quo insunt scripta, pacta, promissa, jurata, quaesita,: dare testimonium sui judicii,; so, laudum suarum,: laboris sui periculique afferre,: ejus rei testimonium esse, quod, etc.,; cf.: ejus rei ipsa verba formulae testimonio sunt,: cui rei mors indigna Palamedis testimonium dat,: quod testimonio sit, non ex verbis aptum pendere jus, sed, etc. : postquam, quae voluerat, dixerat, testimonii loco librum tradidit,: testimonio sunt clarissimi poëtae,: arca testimonii,; et saep.

senses: to summon as a witness, call to witness, invoke, entreat, swear by, appeal to
la:verb:testor.html:
testor, ātus, 1, v. a.
1. testis
.
To be a witness, speak as witness, to bear witness, give evidence, depose, testify, attest any thing.
Lit. (very rare, and not in Cic.; cf. testificor): confiteor: testere licet: signate Quirites,thou canst attest it,: quasi inclamaret aut testaretur locutus est,.—
Transf., in gen., to make known, show, prove, demonstrate; to give to understand, to declare, aver, assert, bear witness to, etc. (class and very freq.): ego quod facio, me pacis, otii, etc. ... causā facere, clamo atque testor,: auctoritatem hujus indicii monumentis publicis,: nunc illa testabor, non me sortilegos ... agnoscere,: testatur isto audiente, se pro communi necessitudine id primum petere,: clarissimā voce se nomen Oppianici ... delaturum esse testatur,: ea quae accidere testatus antea, Dietsch: testatus, quae praestitisset civibus eorum, etc.,: vectigal testandi causā publicum agrum esse imponere,: assiduoque suos gemitu testata dolores,: quod Cicero pluribus et libris et epistulis testatur,: utraeque (venae et arteriae) vim quandam incredibilem artificiosi operis divinique testantur,: sunt Agamemnonias testantia litora curas, (4, 6), 21: ut pura testantur sidera caelo,: verba nos testantia gratos,: carmina raros testantia mores,: campus sepulcris proelia testatur,: numerus autem (saepe enim hoc testandum est) est non modo non poëtice junctus, verum etiam, etc.,; Quint. prooem. § 26; 11, 1, 5.—
In partic., to publish one's last will or testament, to make a will, provide by will for any thing, : cum ignorans nurum ventrem ferre, immemor in testando nepotis decessisset,: quis dubitaret, quin ea voluntas fuisset testantis, ut is non nato filio heres esset,: si exheredatum a se filium pater testatus fuerit elogio,: primipilari seni jam testato,: intestati appellantur, qui cum possent testamentum facere, testati non sunt,; pr.; 49, 14, 45 pr.: nomen testatas intulit in tabulas,i. e. into his will,.—
To call upon or invoke a person or thing as witness (likewise class.): Venus Cyrenensis, testem te testor mihi,: vos, di patrii ac penates, testor, me defendere, etc.,: C. Marii et ceterorum virorum mentis testor, me pro illorum famā propugnandum putare, etc.,: omnes deos, with an obj.-clause, : ego omnes homines deosque testor,: deos immortales,: me potissimum testatus est, se aemulum mearum laudum exstitisse, stuprata per vim Lucretia a regis filio, testata cives, se ipsa interemit, : implorarem sensus vestros, uniuscujusque indulgentiam in suos testarer, etc.,: consulibus deos hominesque testantibus,: Jovem et laesi foederis aras,: vos, aeterni ignes, et non violabile vestrum testor numen,: Theseus infernis, superis testatur Achilles, Hic Ixioniden, ille Menoetiaden,: volnera testor,: id testor deos, Ter Hec. 3, 5, 26: hoc vos, judices, testor,.
Act. collat. form testo, āre, acc. to P.—
Pass. (acc. to I. B.), : cum aliorum monumentis tum Catonis oratione testatum est,shown, proved, attested,; ; —Hence, P. a. in pass. force: testātus, a, um, public, manifest, published (class.): ut res quam maxime clara ac testata esse posset,; . 2, 42, § 104; 1, 16, 48: haec testata sunt atque inlustria,: ut testatum esse velim, de pace quid senserim,: nihil religione testatum,.—Comp.: ut res multorum oculis esset testatior,: quo notior testatiorque virtus ejus esset, : quo testatior esset poena improborum,; .—Sup.: testatissima miracula,.—Hence, adv.: testātō, before witnesses: jussum accipiendum est, sive testato quis, sive verbis, aut per nuntium, jusserit,; cf. ; ; .—
As is well known or evident, .—
After making a will, testate: sive testato, sive intestato, decesserint,.

la:noun:testudo.html:
testūdo, ĭnis, f.
testa
,
a tortoise.
Lit., Pac. ap. ; ; ; ; ; ; ; —Prov.: testudo volat, of any thing impossible,.—
Transf., tortoise-shell.
Used for overlaying or veneering, ; ; ; ; ; . —
From the arched shape of a tortoise-shell.
Of any stringed instrument of music of an arched shape, a lyre, lute, cithern, ; ; ; ; ; ; . —
An arch, vault in buildings (syn.: fornix, camera),, §§ 79 and 161 Müll.; ; ; ; Sisenn. ap. ; . —
In milit. lang., a tortoise, i. e. a covering, shed, shelter so called (cf.: vinea, pluteus), viz.,
Made of wood, for the protection of besiegers, ; ; —
Formed of the shields of the soldiers held over their heads, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; —
The covering of the hedgehog, . —
A head-dress in imitation of a lyre, .

senses: a die with six faces and pips, alike modern-day ones
la:noun:tessera.html:
tessĕra, ae, f., = τέσσερες, α (lon. for τέσσαρες, α, four),
a square, square piece of stone, wood, etc., for various purposes.
Most freq., a die for playing, numbered on all the six sides (while the tali, prop. pastern-bones, were marked only on four sides; v. talus; syn. alea): ludere tesseris,: ut homines ad pilam se aut ad talos aut ad tesseras conferunt,: tesseras jacere,; : in tesserarum prospero jactu,; ; ; : mittere,; ; ; cf. Becker, Gallus, 3, p. 257 sq. (2d ed.).—
In milit. lang., a square tablet on which the watchword was written, a watchword, parole, countersign: tessera per castra a Livio consule data erat, ut, etc.,; ; ; 9, 32, 4; Auct. B. Hisp. 36, 5; : it bello tessera signum, ; : : missam ad se tesseram finxit redeundi,a private token,. — Hence,
Transf., the watchword, signal: militem levi tesserā colligi posse,—
Tessera hospitalis, a tally, token, which was divided between two friends, in order that, by means of it, they or their descendants might always recognize each other (the Greek σύμβολα): Ag. Ego sum ipsus, quem tu quaeris ... Ha. Si ita est, tesseram conferre si vis hospitalem, ; ; : TESSERAM HOSPITALEM CVM EQ FECERVNT,have entered into a bond of friendship,; cf. Becker, Gallus, 2, p. 133 (2d ed.); hence: hic apud nos jam confregisti tesseram,i.e. have broken our friendship,.—
A square tablet or block, a checker for the construction of pavements, ornamenting garments, etc., (al. tessella); ; ; .—
A token, ticket, billet for the distribution of corn or money: frumentariae,; cf. frumenti,; ; and absol., : nummariae,.

la:noun:testificatio.html:
testĭfĭcātĭo, ōnis, f.
testificor
,
a bearing witness, giving testimony, testifying, testification (Ciceron.; whereas testatio is found in the jurists and in Quint.; v. testatio, I.).
Lit.: si ejus rei testificatio tolleretur,; .—In plur., ; .—
Transf., a giving evidence, attestation, proof, evidence: egit causam tuam . . . cum summā testificatione tuorum in se officiorum et amoris erga te sui,: sempiterna repudiatae legationis,.

la:adj:testatior.gloss: having been a witness to, having testified
la:adj:testatior.html:
testātĭo, ōnis. f.
testor
.
A bearing witness (whether orally or in writing), a giving testimony, attesting, testifying (not in Cic., but cf. testificatio), ; ; ; 48, 10, 1; ; ; —
A calling to witness, invoking as witness: inter foederum ruptorum testationem,i.e. during an invocation of the gods as witnesses, (cf. ).

la:verb:testificor.html:
testĭfĭcor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. a. [1. testisfacio].—
To bear witness, give evidence, attest, testify (class.; esp. freq. in Cic.; cf. testor).
Lit.: haec cum maxime testificaretur, in vincula conjectus est,.—With obj.-clause: testificantur illi Quinctium non stitisse,. 25; testificor, denuntio, ante praedico, nihil M. Antonium, etc.,; ; : licet Te memorem dominae testificere tuae,.—With rel.-clause: testificaris, quid dixerim aliquando aut scripserim,.—Absol.: ut statim testificati discederent,.—
Transf., to show, demonstrate, exhibit, publish, bring to light, etc.: testificabar sententiam meam,: amorem meum,: auctam lenitatem suam,: edicto non longam sui absentiam fore,: antiquas opes. : hospitis adventum dei,; cf.: natalem tuum,.—
To call to witness (rare); deos hominesque amicitiamque nostram testificor, me tibi praedixisse, etc., Cael. ap ; , A. 1: homines, deam,; : Stygiae numen aquae,.— Hence,?*! testĭfĭcātus, a, um, in a pass. sense: mihi nota fuit et abs te aliquando testificata tua voluntas omittendae provinciae,made known, averred, exhibited.: mira sed et scaenā testificata loquar,.

senses: one who draws up a will
la:adj:testamentarius.html:
testāmentārĭus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
of or belonging to wills, testamentary.
Adj.: (lex) Cornelia,: adoptio,by will,: hereditates,.—
Subst.: testā-mentārĭus, ii, m.
Ingen., one who draws up a will: si testamentarius contra voluntatem testatoris condicionem detraxit. , §§ 3 and 6; 29, 6, 1; 36, 1, 3 fin.—
In a bad sense, one who forges a will, ; .
